newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA KEEPS WINNING SIDE FOR STH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA KEEPS WINNING SIDE FOR STH AFRICA.

text.p: Australia's cricket selectors on Wednesday stood behind the side which crushed West Indies in the fourth test by choosing an unchanged line-up for the two-month tour of South Africa starting next week.
Selectors rounded out the 14-man squad for South Africa by adding opener Matthew Elliott and right-arm seam bowler Jason Gillespie to the 12 players from the fourth test team.

Despite a dismal run of low scores as an opener, captain Mark Taylor was chosen again in recognition of his leadership skills, acknowledged as a key factor in Australia's 3-1 test series defeat of West Indies this summer.

Australia travelled on Wednesday to Perth to prepare for the anti-climactic fifth and final test starting on Saturday after beating West Indies by an innings and 183 runs in the fourth test in Adelaide on Tuesday.
Elliott returned to club cricket last weekend following undergoing knee surgery after a bizarre mid-pitch collision with Mark Waugh when he was unbeaten on 78 in the second test in Sydney last month.
The 21-year-old Gillespie strained a side muscle during the third test in Melbourne last month but was back bowling in the practice nets this week in Adelaide.
Taylor said he was confident Elliott and Gillespie were fit to play on the South African tour, which he hoped would signal a period of selection stability after recent turmoil.
The Australian selectors dropped opener Michael Slater for the test series against West Indies and made a number of changes for the recent World Series limited overs competition.
Taylor told reporters the fourth test victory had given selectors confidence in the current side.
"It's been a lot more cut-throat for all the guys," a buoyant Taylor said. "It's tough sometimes because it puts a certain edge on the team, a nervous edge."
"But when it works, like it has, it makes the guys better for it because they play under pressure all the time," he said.

"We've had a few changes this summer, but now the guys who have been picked have been told, 'you're the ones that came out ahead of the rest and you've got not just two games or a game, but you've got a two month tour of South Africa to continue to do the business'," he said.

The Australia squad is: Mark Taylor (captain), Ian Healy (vice-captain), Michael Bevan, Andrew Bichel, Greg Blewett, Matthew Elliott, Jason Gillespie, Matthew Hayden, Justin Langer, Glenn McGrath, Paul Reiffel, Shane Warne, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh.
